transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in mostly because I’ve been feeling tired in a way I can’t really explain. I can sleep, and I’m still getting through work, but I feel like I’m running on a low battery before the day even really starts.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the low energy and tiredness?
It’s been about two years and four months now. It really started when I got pulled back into full operational leadership at work.
Have you noticed any changes in how you feel about activities you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with loved ones?

Yeah. For a long time now, most days I’ve had this kind of gray, flat feeling. Things I used to look forward to — fishing, working on the tomatoes, even a church concert — they just feel more like items on a checklist than something I actually enjoy.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… most days, I’d say. It’s not always like I’m crying or anything, but there’s this gray, flat feeling that sits there through a lot of the day. Even things I used to look forward to, like fishing or tending the tomatoes, just feel more like things to get through than things I enjoy.
How much has this feeling affected your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

It’s affected things some, but I’m still managing the main parts of my job. I get the essential work done. But outside of that, I’ve missed routine appointments, the garden’s kind of gotten away from me, and I’ve backed out of some church and community things I used to be pretty dependable for.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not worth much, even when there’s no real reason for it?
Not really, no. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes for letting things slide, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless or guilty for no reason. It’s more just… annoyed with myself, I guess.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

I haven’t really noticed that, no. I’m not pacing around or feeling like I can’t sit still, and I don’t think I’m moving especially slow either. Maybe I’m a little less energetic, but not in that obvious way.
Have you completely stopped doing any of the activities you used to enjoy, or do you still take part in them, even if you don’t get as much out of them?

I haven’t completely stopped, no. I still do some of those things—like fishing sometimes, or tending the tomatoes, or going to a church concert. But for a long time now it’s had this kind of gray, flat feeling most days. Things I used to look forward to feel more like items on a checklist than something I’m really enjoying.
Can you recall if there have been days when nothing — not even the things you usually enjoy — brought you any real sense of pleasure or satisfaction?

Yes, there have been days like that. Even with things I usually like—fishing, working with the tomatoes, going to a church concert—it can feel pretty flat. I’ll still do them, but a lot of the time there’s not much satisfaction in it. It’s more like I’m just checking something off than really enjoying it.
Have there been times when absolutely nothing — not even things you normally care about — gave you any sense of pleasure or joy at all?

Yes… I think so. It’s not every single moment, but for a long time most days have had this gray, flat feeling. Even things I normally care about—like fishing, working with my tomatoes, or going to a church concert—can feel more like I’m just getting through them than actually enjoying them.
Have you had days where you truly didn’t feel any pleasure or interest in anything at all — not even things you normally care about?

Yes, there have been days like that. I mean, I still might go through the motions—go fishing, work on the tomatoes, sit through a church concert—but it doesn’t really land. It just feels gray and flat, like I’m doing it because it’s on the list, not because I’m getting any real pleasure out of it.
Have you had days where even things you normally look forward to, like fishing or working in the garden, felt completely empty or meaningless — like they couldn’t lift your mood at all?

Yes. I know I’ve said it a few ways, but that’s pretty much it. For a long time now, most days have this gray, flat feeling. I can be fishing or out tending the tomatoes, even sitting at a church concert, and it just feels… empty. Like I’m doing it because it’s something I’m supposed to do, not because it actually lifts my mood or gives me much enjoyment.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently, like losing or gaining a noticeable amount without trying?

Yeah… I have noticed some change. My appetite’s been off more days than not. I’ll work through lunch and not even realize I skipped it, then at dinner I just kind of pick at what’s there. My wife mentioned my pants are fitting looser, and I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you noticed any problems with your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything major with that. I still get through work and make the decisions I need to make. Maybe I’m a little slower some days, but nothing that really stands out to me.
Have you ever felt so slowed down that even simple tasks took a lot of effort, or so restless that you couldn’t stay still for more than a few minutes?

Not really, no. I mean, I have days where I feel worn down and it takes some pushing to get going, but I wouldn’t say I’m moving unusually slow or that simple things take forever. And I’m not especially restless either.
Have you felt like your thinking is slowed down, or that it's harder to focus or make decisions, even with simple things?

Like I said, I don’t think so in any big way. I can still focus enough to get through things and make decisions. Maybe I have to push myself a bit on some days, but I haven’t noticed my thinking being really slowed down or simple choices feeling hard.

Have there been any periods lasting at least two months when you felt significantly better or noticed a real improvement in your mood and energy levels, or has it been more of a steady, ongoing struggle without much relief?

It’s been more steady, I’d say. I can’t really point to a stretch of two months or more where I felt a lot better. This started when I got pulled back into full operational leadership, about two years and four months ago, and it’s kind of been ongoing since then.
